title: Hester Panim and the Angels of Peace
summary: "Many evils and troubles": the Gemara's remedies for a wasp and a scorpion, and what it means when Hashem hides His face. The tax collector who would not be helped in time, Rabbi Yehoshua's silent exchange in sign language ("His hand is stretched over us"), how a tzaddik's thought alone can change things, and the angels of peace who wept, with a word on Shalom Aleichem.
key_ideas: Even in hester panim, "His hand is stretched over us."
Help a person before the trouble grows, not after.
A tzaddik's thought alone can affect another person.
Every word a person says, even in private, is recounted before him.
